Can we pin model versions in Dedicated?

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jin Park (Redwood Product), Lena Ortiz (Horizon CTO), Rajiv Menon (SRE), Grace Kim (PM), Tom Alvarez (Data Eng)

Auto-generated summary: walkthrough of console tracing, error analysis, request logs; action items at end.

00:00 - Sofia Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i think we have about 45 minutes, we'll do a quick overview and then demo tracing, error analysis, and request logs - feel free to interrupt.
00:18 - Lena Ortiz: thanks, Sofia. quick context - we're Horizon Health, building a patient triage assistant. latency and PHI concerns are top of mind, and we run a hybrid infra.
00:32 - Marcus Lee: got it, thanks. real quick — are you on cloud-only today or mixed on-prem?
00:40 - Rajiv Menon: mixed, most inference runs on our private cluster but some spike to cloud. also, KMS integration for encryption keys is a hard requirement.
00:50 - Sofia Patel: totally; we'll show both the hosted behaviors and notes on private/KMS. Marcus will share the console and live traces.
01:05 - Marcus Lee: ok switching to screen, here's the Redwood Console. timeline at top, per-route metrics, you can see token-level cost breakdown. forgive me if the slide names are off — sometimes the autogenerated labels get weird.
01:25 - Marcus Lee: so first, tracing. each request creates a trace id, we capture lifecycle events — model selection, routing, kv cache hit/miss, kernel selection, and final response time.
01:40 - Grace Kim: quick question, how granular is kernel selection in the trace? we need to know when quantized fallback happens.
01:52 - Marcus Lee: we record kernel path as an attribute; you'll see entries like "kern_sel: int8-fp16-fallback" in the trace. sometimes logs show "in-t8" if the ASR mis-transcribes, but the attribute is there.
02:10 - Tom Alvarez: and KV cache hits? we need to correlate long tail latency to cache eviction.
02:18 - Marcus Lee: yes, we tag cache operations — "kv_hit" or "kv_miss". in the trace timeline you can hover and see the cache object id; note sometimes the UI truncates long ids, weird transcription there.
02:35 - Lena Ortiz: how about correlation across retries? we have observed retries in our system producing duplicate consumer calls, want to trace back to the original request.
02:44 - Marcus Lee: good point. Redwood links retries with the original trace via a parent_trace_id and a reason tag (e.g., 429-throttle). you can filter traces by parent id in the console.
03:00 - Sofia Patel: jumping to error analysis — Marcus, walk through a common error flow.
03:06 - Marcus Lee: sure. here is an error group view. errors are automatically grouped by stack similarity and model output anomaly. for LLMs we look at divergence from golden prompts and hallucination signals.
03:22 - Rajiv Menon: how noisy is the grouping? we don't want to drown in false positives.
03:28 - Marcus Lee: grouping uses heuristics plus signal thresholds; you can tune sensitivity per route. often customers tune to reduce spurious groups. we also attach sample inputs and outputs to the group so you can triage quickly.
03:45 - Grace Kim: do we get diffs across model versions? our product team wants regression detection for quality.
03:52 - Marcus Lee: yes, we store baseline evals and you can run A/B comparisons — the console will show error rate deltas and per-prompt regressions. that ties into Redwood Optimize but you can run quick checks here.
04:12 - Lena Ortiz: can logs be exported to our S3? compliance requires persistent storage in our bucket.
04:20 - Marcus Lee: absolutely. request-logs export supports streaming to S3 or pushing to a syslog endpoint. retention is configurable; for private deployments you control retention fully. for hosted we offer up to X days by default and an add-on for longer.
04:38 - Tom Alvarez: is the export streaming in real-time or batch?
04:42 - Marcus Lee: we support both. real-time streaming via Kafka/SQS/Syslog, or batch exports on schedule. we'll include the export config doc in the follow-up.
05:00 - Sofia Patel: small note — we'll share SOC2 and the KMS integration guide after this call.
05:07 - Lena Ortiz: great. Rajiv, can you describe your SRE concerns?
05:13 - Rajiv Menon: sure — we care about tail latency, missing cache hits, and opaque failures. we need tracing to surface root cause quickly. also, on private infra, how much of the control plane touches PHI?
05:27 - Marcus Lee: for private deployments, the control plane can be self-managed or a thin plane with no persisted PHI. we'll send more detail. in traces we sanitize PHI by default on hosted; for private you can configure masking rules.
05:45 - Grace Kim: let's jump to the request logs UI.
05:50 - Marcus Lee: this page lists every request with metadata — route, model, latency, tokens in/out, and error codes. you can click into a single request to see the full trace timeline and payloads (payloads are redacted if configured).
06:12 - Marcus Lee: demo searching: i'll filter for route = "patient-triage" and status = 500. you can see groupings by error code and stack trace.
06:28 - Tom Alvarez: the timestamps on the entries look like 2026-04-20T22:00Z, but in our system we use local timezone — can we normalize?
06:35 - Marcus Lee: yes display timezone is configurable per org. exports include timezone info in the header. sometimes the UI truncates the timezone string in certain browsers, weird bug. we'll file that.
06:50 - Lena Ortiz: what's the overhead of tracing on latency? we can't add more than 5% to p95.
06:58 - Marcus Lee: tracing sampling is adaptive; for hot routes we sample lower and for error traces we force capture. overhead is minimal — typically sub 3% for sampling-only. for full payload capture you can see more CPU but we recommend selective capture.
07:18 - Rajiv Menon: can we trigger full trace on 5xxs only?
07:22 - Marcus Lee: yes that's a common policy. we'll show the policy editor in a sec.
07:30 - Marcus Lee: switching to policy editor — here's a rule: if status >= 500 then capture full trace and payload and stream to our secure S3 destination. you can also add attributes like "session_id" to correlate.
07:48 - Grace Kim: how do we search across traces for a specific user id? we want to see a user's session across multiple calls.
07:55 - Marcus Lee: you can add custom attributes in the SDK or header, then query by attribute. there's also a correlation view that stitches requests by attribute value. note: make sure PII is not logged; we recommend hashing user ids before sending.
08:12 - Lena Ortiz: what about role-based access to these logs? compliance requires product and security to have different visibility.
08:20 - Marcus Lee: console supports RBAC: you can limit access to request payloads, or mask fields per role. SAML/SSO integrates with our RBAC mappings.
08:30 - Tom Alvarez: show us the error grouping UI again.
08:33 - Marcus Lee: here — errors grouped, with counts, first/last seen, sample exemplars. clicking into a group shows the stack, related traces, and a timeline of occurrences. we can correlate to model rollouts.
08:50 - Grace Kim: speaking of rollouts, if a model rollback happens, can we re-run traces against the previous model?
08:57 - Marcus Lee: we store model version id in traces; you can filter by model version and re-run comparisons. for reruns you typically pull the request inputs and run them in a safe sandbox. Redwood has a replay tool (subject to permissions) to re-invoke requests against a pinned model.
09:18 - Sofia Patel: small aside — competitor question: some teams compare us to Bedrock and OpenAI for managed endpoints; we usually come up on economics and private deployment flexibility.
09:33 - Lena Ortiz: yeah cost is important. can you show token-level cost per request in the trace?
09:40 - Marcus Lee: yep, cost breakdown shows model compute, token count, and approximate infra cost. in Dedicated you can set a cost model for internal showbacks.
09:52 - Rajiv Menon: about private deployment — what's the minimum footprint? we have constrained GPU resources.
10:00 - Marcus Lee: minimum depends on model size; for 30B class models we recommend at least 4xA10s; smaller quantized variants can run on fewer GPUs. we can share a sizing guide.
10:15 - Lena Ortiz: is quantization auditable? we need to be sure outputs still meet medical quality bar.
10:22 - Marcus Lee: Redwood Optimize can evaluate quality regressions after quantization; in the console you can see per-prompt quality diffs. we'll demo Optimize separately if you want.
10:35 - Grace Kim: back to debugging — can we create alerts from the console for an uptick in error groups?
10:42 - Marcus Lee: yes, alerts tie into error groups and can notify Slack, PagerDuty, or email. thresholds are configurable and we have prebuilt templates for common patterns.
10:55 - Tom Alvarez: a quick call-out — how do you handle PII in traces when customers want full payload capture for debugging?
11:02 - Marcus Lee: default is masking; for customers who opt-in for full capture, we require contractual terms and additional controls like HSM-stored keys and ephemeral retention. we'll route this to the security review.
11:18 - Sofia Patel: ok now i'm going to walk through a live debugging flow — find a 500 spike from this morning.
11:25 - Marcus Lee: selecting date range and filtering to patient-triage route. i see a spike at 09:12 UTC, p95 went to 4.2s. i'll open a sample trace.
11:42 - Marcus Lee: trace shows a kv_miss at model load time and then a kernel fallback to a slower path, that added 1.8s. you can see the kernel attribute and the timeline.
12:00 - Rajiv Menon: so that indicates cache eviction followed by cold kernel selection. do you expose cache eviction metrics over time?
12:07 - Marcus Lee: yes, we have a cache dashboard with hit ratio and evictions per minute. we can correlate evictions to resizes or restarts.
12:18 - Lena Ortiz: does the cache persist across restarts in Dedicated?
12:22 - Marcus Lee: yes if you have a shared KV cache store; otherwise cold starts happen. that's why we recommend warmers or persistent cache layers.
12:33 - Grace Kim: something transcribed oddly in the trace — the model name shows as "red-bread v2" in one of the traces, is that a Redwood model name?
12:42 - Marcus Lee: haha yeah sometimes the ASR mis-reads; that's likely "redwood-v2" but we'll double-check. product names can get mangled in the transcript, noted.
12:55 - Tom Alvarez: what about request replays — do they include original headers? we need that to reproduce auth-flows.
13:02 - Marcus Lee: replay includes headers you opt to capture; by default auth tokens are redacted. you can selectively retain headers for debugging in a secure replay environment.
13:18 - Lena Ortiz: can we hook the console traces into our internal tracing system like Datadog?
13:24 - Marcus Lee: yes we ship spans to Datadog/OTLP and can attach trace ids so you get a unified picture.
13:35 - Grace Kim: walk us through a compliance scenario — someone requests audit logs for a given timeframe.
13:42 - Marcus Lee: you can export request logs for a timeframe; exports include immutable headers with audit trail. for Private, you host the logs. for Hosted, we provide signed exports. we'll include the audit export playbook.
14:00 - Sofia Patel: time check — about 30 minutes left, let's cover remaining items and then confirm next steps.
14:06 - Marcus Lee: quick demo: creating a custom trace sampling policy. here i add a rule: sample 100% for route patient-triage where risk_flag=true. then i show how to preview which requests would be captured.
14:30 - Rajiv Menon: preview looks good. how do we surface which requests have PHI so we can mask?
14:36 - Marcus Lee: Redwood supports content classifiers and regex masking; you can also send a header marking PHI presence and the policy can automatically redact.
14:48 - Grace Kim: awesome. any limitations on payload size for request logs?
14:53 - Marcus Lee: we cap payload capture size by default (2MB), larger payloads get truncated with a note. you can request increased caps for private deployments.
15:05 - Lena Ortiz: about encryption — we need customer-managed keys for logs at rest.
15:10 - Marcus Lee: yes KMS/HSM integrations are supported; for hosted we integrate with customer KMS in supported clouds; for private you manage keys fully.
15:25 - Tom Alvarez: one more — how do you reconcile model rollouts with error spikes? any automation?
15:31 - Marcus Lee: we have rollout policies that can auto-rollback if error rate increases beyond threshold. console shows the rollout and can trigger fallback to previous model version automatically.
15:45 - Sofia Patel: ok coming to the end — let's recap next steps.
15:49 - Lena Ortiz: quick note on timeline: compliance review by 4/30, pilot decision by mid-May.
16:00 - Sofia Patel: action items: we'll send SOC2/security docs, provision a trial org with tracing enabled, Marcus will run a 24h request-logs export and demo the export format, and we schedule POC scoping for May 4th.
16:18 - Marcus Lee: i'll also include a short runbook for replaying failed requests and the sizing guide.
16:25 - Grace Kim: can you also include Optimize notes on quantization quality checks?
16:30 - Jin Park: absolutely, I'll add a short Optimize primer.
16:35 - Rajiv Menon: one ask — can you include sample queries for identifying cache-eviction driven latency?
16:42 - Marcus Lee: yes I'll include the sample queries and the dashboard JSON you can import.
16:50 - Sofia Patel: cool, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the links.
16:55 - Lena Ortiz: thank you — useful session.
17:00 - meeting end

Notes: minor transcription glitches (product names sometimes mis-typed), some speaker labels condensed. Shared links mentioned: security deck (link: https://redwood.ai/security-deck), export config doc (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/export-config), sizing guide (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/sizing-guide).
